title: Ellipse rigidity from a continuous physical collar of smooth caustics
exact_target: Let a bounded planar billiard table have a C-infinity strictly convex boundary with everywhere positive curvature. If a whole inner boundary collar is continuously foliated by individually C-infinity strictly convex closed caustics, with no differentiability of the transverse foliation assumed, must the boundary be an ellipse?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
Let a bounded planar billiard table have a C-infinity strictly convex boundary with everywhere positive curvature. If a whole inner boundary collar is continuously foliated by individually C-infinity strictly convex closed caustics, with no differentiability of the transverse foliation assumed, must the boundary be an ellipse?

\subsection{Short English statement}
Let a bounded planar billiard table have a C-infinity strictly convex boundary with everywhere positive curvature. If a whole inner boundary collar is continuously foliated by individually C-infinity strictly convex closed caustics, with no differentiability of the transverse foliation assumed, must the boundary be an ellipse?
